alert_news.title: India’s First Virtual Zoo – 14D Immersive Experience
bullets: India’s first virtual zoo, a 14D immersive experience, located at Kamala Nehru Prani Sangrahalaya, Indore, Madhya Pradesh.
Built by Indore Municipal Corporation under a PPP model, covering 8,000 sq ft and costing ₹4.6 crore.
Features a 14D cinema theatre with waterproof screen, digital jungle safari, 3D dome, and sensory effects (water, wind, fog, smells, moving seats).

alert_news.title: Karnataka to launch AI education from Class 6 and establish India's first government-owned AI university
bullets: Karnataka will introduce AI education from Class 6 through AI Akshara Abhiyana and Coding Gurukula programmes.
The state is also establishing India's first government-owned AI university in Bengaluru.
AI certificate courses are slated to launch in January 2027, with AI hubs planned across Karnataka.

alert_news.title: India’s First Government Hospital with AI‑Based Pneumatic Tube System – Dr Marri Chenna Reddy TIMS
bullets: India’s first government hospital to install an AI‑based pneumatic tube system, at Dr Marri Chenna Reddy TIMS, Telangana.
Hospital spans 22.6 acres, houses 1,082 beds (300 ICU), 31 major OT, 6 minor OT and advanced diagnostic labs.
AI pneumatic tube transports blood samples and medical reports between wards, labs and pharmacy in 1–2 minutes.

alert_news.title: India's first virtual zoo opens in Indore with 14‑D cinema and virtual jungle safari facilities
bullets: India’s first virtual zoo inaugurated at Kamala Nehru Prani Sangrahalaya, Indore, Madhya Pradesh.
Developed under a PPP model at a cost of ₹4.5 crore, it houses a 14‑D cinema, a 3‑D dome theatre and a digital jungle safari.
The 8,000‑sq‑ft facility opened to the public on 17 August 2026.

alert_news.title: Indore Gets India's First Virtual Zoo
bullets: India’s first virtual zoo established at the Kamala Nehru Prani Sangrahalaya, Indore, Madhya Pradesh.
The 8,000‑sq‑ft complex, built under a Public‑Private Partnership, cost ₹4.5 crore and features a 14‑D cinema, 3‑D dome theatre and a digital jungle safari.
It opened on 17 August 2026, offering immersive wildlife experiences through advanced projection and sensory effects.

alert_news.title: Indias First Sports AI Center Launches at LNIPE Gwalior
bullets: India’s first Sports AI Centre inaugurated at Lakshmibai National Institute of Physical Education (LNIPE), Gwalior.
The centre will use AI to analyse athletes’ physique, movement and performance for early talent identification and training optimisation.
It is part of the Sports Education Technology Upgradation initiative and is expected to be fully operational by November 2026.

alert_news.title: Karnataka Introduces QR Code‑Based Food Safety Complaint System – First in India
bullets: Karnataka becomes the first Indian state to deploy QR codes outside hotels and pharmacies for real‑time food safety complaints.
The system allows citizens to scan a code and file complaints directly; 60 hotels have already received notices.

alert_news.title: India's 1st Virtual Zoo Lets You Experience The Jungle In 14D Without Leaving Your Seat
bullets: India’s first virtual zoo located in Indore, Madhya Pradesh, built by Indore Municipal Corporation under a PPP model at a cost of ₹4.6 crore.

The 8,000‑sq‑ft facility houses a 14D cinema theatre with a waterproof screen imported from South Korea, offering 14 real‑life effects such as water sprays, wind blasts, fog, bubbles, smells and moving seats.

alert_news.title: CM Revanth Reddy to inaugurate AI-equipped Dr Marri Chenna Reddy TIMS today
bullets: India’s first government hospital to install an AI‑based pneumatic tube system, located at Dr Marri Chenna Reddy TIMS in Telangana and built by the state government.

The system moves blood samples and medical reports between wards, labs and pharmacy in 1–2 minutes; the hospital spans 22.6 acres with 1,082 beds, 300 ICU beds, 31 major and 6 minor operation theatres.

alert_news.title: How Karnataka will create 1 lakh new jobs - HR Katha
bullets: Bengaluru will host India’s first government‑owned AI university, part of Karnataka’s AI education initiative announced by the state government.
The university, to be established under the state’s Udyoga Sankalpa and Udyoga Nidhi schemes, aims to advance AI research and education across the country.

alert_news.title: Karnataka CM Announces AI Akshara Abhiyana, Coding Gurukula for School Students from Class 6
bullets: India's first government-owned AI University to be established in Bengaluru, Karnataka.
The university will be set up by the state government, marking the first of its kind in India.

alert_news.title: India's First Lunar Landing: Chandrayaan-3 Successfully Lands Vikram Lander on Moon
bullets: India's first lunar landing was achieved by Chandrayaan-3 in 2023, with the successful landing of the Vikram lander and deployment of the Pragyan rover near the lunar south polar region.
This marked a historic achievement, making India the fourth country to achieve a lunar landing after the United States, Russia, and China.
The Chandrayaan-3 mission demonstrated India's capability to explore and operate in space, a significant milestone in the country's space journey.

alert_news.title: India's First Satellite: Aryabhata Launched in 1975
bullets: India's first satellite, Aryabhata, was launched on April 19, 1975, from the Volgograd Launch Station (Kapustin Yar) in the Soviet Union using a Kosmos-3M launch vehicle.
Aryabhata marked the beginning of India's journey towards developing its own expertise in spacecraft and space science.
The satellite was a significant milestone in India's space programme, paving the way for the development of indigenous launch vehicles and satellites.

alert_news.title: India's First AI-Powered Household-Level Skill Census Model
bullets: India's first AI-powered, household-level skill census model was conducted in H/West ward of Mumbai Suburban district, covering Bandra West, Khar West, and Santacruz West.
This model aims to understand the real employment potential of urban population and bridge the gap between skills and employment through certification and women's workforce participation.
The survey is expected to create Maharashtra's blueprint for future livelihood intelligence.

alert_news.title: India's First Government-Owned AI University to be Established in Bengaluru
bullets: India's first government-owned AI university to be established in Bengaluru, Karnataka, marking a significant milestone in the country's AI education sector.

The university will be a pioneering institution in India, focusing on artificial intelligence education and research, and will play a crucial role in preparing the country's youth for the emerging technological era.
The establishment of this university is a testament to the government's commitment to promoting AI education and innovation in the country.

alert_news.title: India's First 440 Space Technology Startups Registered
bullets: India has around 440 space technology startups registered, as per the DPIIT Start-up India Portal.
IN-SPACe has granted 113 authorisations to 52 Non-Government Entities (NGEs) for various space activities, out of which 18 are start-ups.
Private investment in India's space sector surged nearly six-fold, climbing from USD 100.5 million in 2021-22 to USD 618.5 million by March 31, 2026.

alert_news.title: India's First Vande Bharat Freight Train Clocks 130 kmph in Trial
bullets: India's first Vande Bharat freight train was tested at 130 kmph on the Kota-Rohal Khurd section of West Central Railway.

The train was developed by Chennai-based Integral Coach Factory and is equipped with advanced propulsion and braking systems, roller floor system, automatic wide sliding doors, temperature-controlled facilities, CCTV surveillance, and fire detection systems.
The trial was conducted as part of technical testing by teams from Research Designs and Standards Organisation (RDSO) and Integral Coach Factory (ICF) to assess the train's performance at high speed.

alert_news.title: India's First Vande Bharat Freight Train Completes High-Speed Safety And Braking Trials
bullets: India's first Vande Bharat freight train, manufactured at Chennai's Integral Coach Factory, has a maximum operational speed of 160 kmph and a total payload capacity of 395 tonnes.

The 16-coach prototype features modern safety features including fire detection systems, CCTV surveillance, and the Indian Railways' automated anti-collision system KAVACH, with automatic door locking at 5 kmph and secured doors required for movement.
The high-speed freight service is expected to benefit sectors such as e-commerce, pharmaceuticals, agriculture, and express logistics, with faster deliveries critical for business operations.
